records.title: Adobe Experience Platform: innovations and momentum

records.core_message: Our business is a self-reinforcing flywheel where content creation and digital delivery feed each other, powered by a central Data & AI engine, creating a compounding competitive advantage.

shows.specific_content: A circular diagram illustrating a business flywheel. At the center is 'Data & AI'. The cycle shows 'Creativity & productivity' leading to 'Digital experiences', which is then improved by 'Analysis & optimization' and 'Variation & personalization', feeding back into the loop. Each stage is illustrated with product UI mockups.

It also lists customer segments in the footer: Students, Consumers, Communicators, Creative Professionals, Developers, SMBs, Enterprises.

records.abstract_pattern: This is a 'virtuous cycle' or 'flywheel' pattern used to illustrate a self-reinforcing business model. It shows how distinct parts of a platform or business (e.g., creation, distribution, consumption) feed each other in a continuous loop. A central engine, often data, AI, or a core technology, powers the cycle and gets stronger with each turn. Any company can use this to demonstrate how its components create a synergistic effect, leading to a compounding advantage and a strong competitive moat.
works_for: Our marketplace attracts more sellers, which increases selection, which attracts more buyers, which in turn attracts more sellers.
More users on our platform generate more data, which improves our AI models, which delivers a better product, which attracts more users.
Our developer tools enable more apps, which attracts more end-users, whose usage data helps us improve the tools.
Increased logistics density lowers our cost per delivery, allowing us to offer lower prices, which drives more volume.
Great content attracts subscribers, whose engagement data informs new content, which attracts more subscribers.
Our open-source community improves the core product, which attracts enterprise customers, whose revenue funds further development.
The more people use our payment network, the more valuable it becomes for both merchants and consumers.

variable_elements.primary_metric: Central Engine (e.g., Data & AI, Marketplace Liquidity, Community)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: Cycle Stages (e.g., Creation, Distribution, Analysis)
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self-reinforcing system (internal components)

must_have: A clear definition of the stages in your business's value loop
Identification of the central engine that powers the loop (e.g., data, network, technology)
A narrative explaining how the output of one stage becomes the input for another
data_requirements.data_shape_needed: cyclical_narrative
data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 3+ distinct stages in the cycle

ideal_for: Explaining how different product lines create synergistic value together.
Demonstrating a sustainable competitive advantage (moat) that is hard to replicate.
Articulating the core business model to investors, especially for a platform company.
Showing how data or a core technology is the central driver of the entire business.
Justifying why the whole is greater than the sum of its parts.
avoid_when: Your business is linear (e.g., simple reselling) with no feedback loops.
Your product lines operate in silos with no demonstrable synergy.
You cannot clearly articulate the stages or the engine that drives the cycle.

records.title: Monetizing our innovations – Adobe's growth algorithm

records.core_message: By using our own data-driven methodology as 'customer zero' over the last decade, we've systematically built capabilities that drove our revenue from $4B to over $20B while expanding operating margins, proving the power of our approach.

records.abstract_pattern: This is a 'company-as-case-study' journey pattern. Any company can use this to show its own transformation over a long period, connecting a series of internal strategic initiatives and capability developments to a significant, positive business outcome (like revenue growth and margin expansion). The core idea is to establish ultimate credibility by demonstrating 'we used our own medicine to succeed,' proving the value and scalability of the company's core product, methodology, or platform.

variable_elements.primary_metric: A major business KPI showing significant growth (e.g., Revenue, ARR, Customer Count)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: A measure of efficiency or profitability (e.g., Operating Margin, CAC Payback, Gross Margin)
variable_elements.time_dimension: A multi-year timeline showing progression and evolution
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over a long period of time

A list of key strategic initiatives or product developments over that time period

Demonstrating a deep, hard-to-replicate competitive moat built over time.
avoid_when: You are an early-stage company without a long history.
Your own internal use of your product is not a compelling success story.
The connection between your initiatives and the outcome is weak or hard to prove.

variable_elements.primary_metric: Top-of-funnel acquisition metric (e.g., traffic, sign-ups, downloads)
variable_elements.secondary_metric: Downstream business impact metric (e.g., MAU, conversion rate, revenue)
variable_elements.time_dimension: Period-over-period growth (Y/Y, Q/Q) and point-in-time totals
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Self over time and comparison of a new initiative against an internal benchmark (e.g., average feature adoption).

ideal_for: Proving a new feature is a strategic growth driver, not just a gimmick.

records.core_message: Adobe's Digital Experience platform creates a complete value chain for customers, starting with acquiring new users, then managing them at scale, and ultimately driving significant revenue growth and ROI.

shows.specific_content: A three-column layout illustrating a customer value journey, with each column topped by a green upward arrow. records.abstract_pattern: This is a 'value chain' or 'flywheel' pattern that breaks a process into distinct, sequential stages. It's used to tell a story of how a customer achieves a significant outcome using the company's product. The pattern starts with an initial action or benefit (e.g., acquisition), moves to an intermediate scaling or deepening phase (e.g., platform adoption), and culminates in a final, quantifiable business result (e.g., revenue, ROI). Any company can use this to explain how their integrated solution creates compounding value, making the journey from feature adoption to financial impact clear and tangible.
works_for: Our security platform turns initial threat detection into automated response, ultimately reducing incident resolution time by 90%.
Our developer tool starts with code analysis, integrates into the CI/CD pipeline, and results in a 50% reduction in production bugs.
Our HR software simplifies onboarding, improves employee engagement, and demonstrably lowers staff turnover.

Our marketing automation tool helps acquire subscribers, nurtures them with personalized content, and converts them into paying customers.
Our data platform ingests raw data, transforms it into clean datasets, and powers business intelligence dashboards that drive better decisions.

variable_elements.primary_metric: The final, ultimate business outcome for the customer (e.g., Revenue, ROI, Cost Savings).
variable_elements.secondary_metric: Intermediate metrics representing progress through the value chain (e.g., New Customers, Data Points Managed, Features Adopted).
variable_elements.time_dimension: Progression through logical stages (e.g., Stage 1 -> Stage 2 -> Stage 3).
variable_elements.comparison_basis: Implicitly compares the 'before' state (without the solution) to the 'after' state (with the solution's benefits).

must_have: A clear, multi-stage customer value story (typically 3 stages)
A key metric for the final outcome (e.g., revenue, savings, efficiency gain)
Supporting metrics or qualitative examples for intermediate stages
Visual representations (mockups, screenshots, icons) for each stage

data_requirements.minimum_data_points: 3 distinct stages, each with at least one proof point (qualitative or quantitative).

ideal_for: Explaining how your platform delivers tangible ROI to customers.
Illustrating the customer journey from initial adoption to full value realization.
Justifying a premium price by showing a clear path to value.
Showcasing the synergy between different product features or modules.
Telling a 'how it works' story to investors or potential enterprise buyers.
Demonstrating a product-led growth (PLG) motion that leads to enterprise value.
avoid_when: Your product is a simple, single-feature tool without a multi-stage value story.
You only have one key metric to show and don't need to explain the 'how'.
You lack clear evidence or metrics for the intermediate steps in the journey.

records.title: Digital Experience: driving the top-line with personalization at scale

records.core_message: Adobe is expanding its massive market opportunity with a dual strategy: increasing value for high-end users ('raising the ceiling') and broadening its user base by making products more accessible ('lowering the floor').

shows.specific_content: A diagram showing Adobe's three main product clouds (Document, Creative, Experience) with their respective 2024 Total Addressable Market (TAM) sizes. This is framed by a 'Raise the ceiling' and 'Lower the floor' metaphor, with bullet points explaining the strategies for each: adding more value for existing users and attracting more new users.

records.abstract_pattern: Any company can use this pattern to showcase a dual-axis growth strategy for market expansion. It combines large market size numbers (TAM) with a memorable strategic framework, typically a metaphor like 'raising the ceiling and lowering the floor'. This demonstrates a comprehensive plan to capture the market from two directions: by increasing the value extracted from the high-end or core market (upselling, premium features) and simultaneously expanding the user base by making the product more accessible to a broader, entry-level audience (democratization, simpler tools, lower price points). This 'pincer movement' approach shows a mature and robust plan for both deepening and widening market penetration.
works_for: Our strategy is to add premium AI features for power users while making our basic version free to attract millions of new users.
We're growing by making our enterprise platform more powerful while also launching a self-serve version for SMBs.
We are expanding our market by both upselling advanced modules to our existing customers and creating a simpler entry-level product.
Our financial model grows through both high-value enterprise contracts and high-volume individual subscriptions.
We're capturing the entire market by serving both professional creators with our pro suite and casual users with our mobile app.

Our path to market leadership involves both deepening our enterprise footprint and widening our reach to individual developers.

A clear strategic narrative for increasing value per customer (upsell/premium features)

Your strategy is purely focused on one dimension (e.g., only enterprise sales).
You don't have credible, defensible TAM numbers to support your claims.
